newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai newspaper urges long-term stock view.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai newspaper urges long-term stock view.

text.p: The Shanghai Securities News on Sunday urged investors to take a long-term view to investing in shares and not be rattled by the dramatic falls on the Chinese stock markets over the past week.
The newspaper said the declines in share prices since Beijing launched a crackdown last Monday had pulled the markets back into more sensible territory.
"The falls in share prices have been big this week, but every investor must remain clear-headed. This correction brings the balance of prices back to a reasonable level," the newspaper said.
It said long-term investment strategies were the answer to the investor's problem of dealing with risk in the share markets.
"Given that the overall economic climate in China is continuing to improve, the only means by which we can offset risk is to hold to a long-term investment strategy," it said.

On Friday, Shanghai's domestic A share index closed at 922.34 points, down 20 percent on the previous Friday's close of 1163.050, while the foreign currency B index was down 3.84 percent to 63.743 points from 66.291 the previous Friday.
In Shenzhen, the A share index nosedived 29.07 percent on the week to 328.96 points, while the B index lost 15.94 percent to 125.56.

The falls followed the publication of a commentary in the People's Daily in Beijing saying the stock markets were dangerously overheated and warning that the government would not step in to help investors if they fell.
